spec.description: Returns the last 1000 trades by default.

pair.description: Asset pair to get data for.

assetVersion.description: Controls whether response keys use Kraken's internal names or display names. Omitted (default): internal names are used. `assetVersion=1`: display names are used. Only `assetVersion=1` is currently supported.

since.description: Return trade data since given timestamp.

count.description: Return specific number of trades, up to 1000.

asset_class.description: This parameter is required on requests for non-crypto pairs, i.e. use `tokenized_asset` for xstocks.

response.title: TradesResultFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

result.title: TradesResult
result.description: Trades keyed by pair, plus the polling cursor.

last.description: ID to be used as `since` when polling for new trade data.

additionalProperties.description: This pair's recent trades, oldest first.

items.title: TradeEntry
items.description: One trade `[price, volume, time, buy/sell, market/limit, miscellaneous, trade_id]`.

prefixItems.title: time
prefixItems.description: Trade time, Unix timestamp with sub-second precision.

notes: No pagination block: `since`/`last` is an incremental-update cursor over a live, unbounded trade feed (there is no terminal page -- `last` is always present, even when caught up to real time), not a bounded collection this format's `token` strategy's `absent_cursor` terminator can describe.

`since` (and its paired response field `last`, the same value) declares `format: "epoch-nanos"` (rule 3): confirmed live against `/0/public/Trades` on 2026-08-21 (a returned `last` of `1786622308334567536`, 19 digits, matching wall-clock nanosecond-epoch magnitude) and reconfirmed against the recorded `examples/default.response.json` (`"last": "1786622308334567536"`) -- renders to the client core's `TimestampNanos` (`typed_core.times.EpochConverter.nanoseconds()`).
